subtopics.title: Identify mutually exclusive events
subtopics.exposition: Two events are called mutually exclusive if they cannot occur at the same time. For mutually exclusive events, whenever an outcome of an experiment is in the first event it cannot also be in the second event, and vice versa. Another way of saying that two events are mutually exclusive is that the two event sets, A and B, cannot have any elements in common. In the Venn diagram of mutually exclusive events, the intersection has no elements. To show that two events are mutually exclusive, first draw the sample space and the two events. Then determine the intersection of the two events; if there are no elements in common in A and B, the events are mutually exclusive. The book writes the condition that the event sets have no elements in common as P(A∩B)=∅, where ∅ denotes the empty set.

subtopics.title: Add probabilities, exclusive events
subtopics.exposition: For mutually exclusive events, the probability of the union is the sum of the probabilities of the events. For mutually exclusive events A and B, P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B).

claims.claim: Two events are called mutually exclusive if they cannot occur at the same time.
For mutually exclusive events, whenever an outcome of an experiment is in the first event it cannot also be in the second event, and vice versa.
Another way of saying that two events are mutually exclusive is that the two event sets, A and B, cannot have any elements in common.
The book writes the condition that the event sets have no elements in common as P(A∩B)=∅, where ∅ denotes the empty set.
In the Venn diagram of mutually exclusive events, the intersection has no elements.
To show that two events are mutually exclusive, first draw the sample space and the two events.
Then determine the intersection of the two events; if there are no elements in common in A and B, the events are mutually exclusive.
For mutually exclusive events, the probability of the union is the sum of the probabilities of the events.
For mutually exclusive events A and B, P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B).
The relationship P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B) is true for mutually exclusive events only.
